open_questions: Confirm FY2025 GAAP OCF minus capex is the right owner-cash starting point vs company-reported adjusted free cash flow.
Ticker change **MMC → MRSH** (Feb 2026): verify price history and index inclusion.
First Marvin dive; no prior stance to preserve.
thesis: Marsh & McLennan Companies is a global professional services firm organized in two segments: **Risk and Insurance Services** (Marsh brokerage, Guy Carpenter reinsurance) and **Consulting** (Mercer health and wealth, Marsh Management Consulting). **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$27.0 billion** and operating income **$6.2 billion** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260209_rpt20251231_acc0000062709_26_000022.htm`). **[Fact]** The company earns fees and commissions placing insurance and advising on risk, plus consulting mandates; it also earns **fiduciary interest income** on client premiums held in trust (**$403 million** in FY2025), which is separate from brokerage fees. **[Fact]** Common stock trades on the NYSE under ticker **MRSH** (symbol change from MMC effective February 2026 per `8-K_20260219_rpt20260219_acc0001193125_26_059544.htm`).
why_market_wrong: The stock may look like a mature, fully priced broker at roughly **19 times** trailing earnings while understating durable mid-single-digit organic growth and high cash conversion. **[Inference]** After the **MRSH** ticker change, index and data-feed friction may keep some screens on legacy **MMC** symbols, leaving a short-lived attention discount. **[Inference]** Investors may treat **2024** cash flow as normal when **$8.5 billion** went to the **Thrive** acquisition (`PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired` in the 10-K cash flow statement), making **FY2025** free cash look like a one-time spike rather than a repeatable **~$5 billion** annual level.
